parole.testo: Uncertain. Bulgarian Etymological Dictionary lists three possible origins: * Derived from глух (gluh, “deaf”) + -ец (-ec), effectively cognate with Polish głuszec (“capercaillie”), Czech hlušec (“capercaillie”), Ukrainian глуше́ць (hlušécʹ, “wood grouse”), Belarusian глушэ́ц (hlušéc, “wood grouse”).

parole.significato: polytonous gray (with varying shades of gray)
parole.testo: According to Georgiev (BER), of Thracian origin, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *g⁽ʷ⁾ʰreh₁wos (the shift of Thracian *-ē- to Bulgarian -и- (-i-) is also reflected in Bulgarian Пловдив (Plovdiv), from an earlier Latin Pulpudēva), cognate with Proto-Germanic *grēwaz and Latin rāvus. Also inherite

parole.significato: concave form (pit, groove, dike) used for soothing hazardous materials such as quicklime or live coals
parole.testo: Of substrate origin (Thracian?), cognate/related to Romanian groapă (“hole, pit”), Albanian gropë (“pit”). Probably ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *gʰrep-, a variant of *gʰrebʰ- (“to scoop”). Doublet of гроб (grob, “grave”).
By surface analysis, кате́ря (katérja, “to climb”) + -ица (-ica), probably of peripheral proto-Slavic origin or borrowed from Thracian. Cognate with Albanian ketër (“squirrel”).

Likely from an unattested Old Bulgarian root *кате́рь (*katérʹ, “squirrel”), cf. катеричка. In turn from Thracian *kater-, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)koktér or *(s)kaktér from the roots *(s)kok- (“to jump”) or *(s)kat- (“to jump”) respectively.

parole.significato: emmer, farro (hulled wheat of genus Triticum)
parole.testo: Of substrate origin (Thracian?), cognate with Ancient Greek ἔλῠμος (élŭmos, “millet”)

Paleo-Balkan substrate word of Thracian origin, likely borrowed from the definite form of Albanian rrufé. Compare Ancient Greek ῥομφαία (rhomphaía, “spear, javelin; sword”) and Latin rhomphaea, rumpia.
Of Thracian or Dacian origin (see the etymology of Carpathian mountains). Cognate with Macedonian карпа (karpa). Alternatively, from Albanian karpë.
